name: OptiMUS (Optimization Modeling Using Solvers and LLMs)
one_liner: An LLM translates natural-language optimization problems into Mixed-Integer Linear Programs and Gurobi solver code, repairs bugs from runtime errors, and solves the model to optimality.

loop.proposes: Mathematical objective and constraint formulations plus executable Gurobi Python code, generated by specialized GPT-4 agents
loop.judged_by: The Gurobi MILP solver and automated checks that surface runtime errors from executing the generated code
loop.steers: Runtime errors from executing the generated code go back to the formulator or programmer agents.

headline_result: At ICML 2024, OptiMUS solved 78.8% of NL4OPT (vs 64.2% for Chain-of-Experts), 66.7% of ComplexOR (vs 38.1%), and 72.0% of the authors' graduate-level NLP4LP benchmark (vs 53.1%). Removing the solver-guided debugging loop in ablations dropped NLP4LP accuracy from 71.6% to 58.2%.
caveat: Gurobi certifies the exact optimum of the generated MILP, not that the MILP faithfully captures every nuance of the English prompt. If the model writes a plausible but semantically wrong constraint that still compiles and solves feasibly, the solver optimizes the wrong problem.
beyond_harness_note: Instead of asking the LLM to guess numeric variable assignments, the LLM compiles the problem into a formal MILP and hands the combinatorial search and optimality certificate to Gurobi.
generative_model: GPT-4 (frozen), structured across formulator, programmer and evaluator agents with a connection graph
algorithmic_authority: Gurobi Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solver plus automated execution checks

sources.title: OptiMUS: Scalable Optimization Modeling with (MI)LP Solvers and Large Language Models (ICML 2024)

verification.notes: Verified against AhmadiTeshnizi, Gao and Udell, ICML 2024 (arXiv:2402.10172). Confirmed NL4OPT 78.8% vs 64.2% CoE, ComplexOR 66.7% vs 38.1% CoE, NLP4LP 72.0% vs 53.1% CoE, and debugging-loop ablation 71.6% vs 58.2%.
